metaDescription: Own minerals near Wellston, MI on the Manistee/Wexford line? We explain what's actually under your parcel and give you a real offer, no gimmicks.
heroLead: Wellston sits near the Manistee-Wexford county line, deep in the Manistee National Forest, in ground where mineral ownership is old and drilling history is thin compared to the Antrim counties to the northeast.
intro: If you've got a mineral interest tied to land around Wellston, it likely came down through a family that owned timber or farm ground here generations back — the kind of interest that gets mentioned once at Thanksgiving and then forgotten about for years. Nobody's getting rich off a Wellston-area royalty check, and we won't pretend otherwise. What we will do is look honestly at whether there's anything of value there and what it's actually worth if there is.
We buy mineral and royalty interests in Manistee County, including around Wellston. If your interest turns out to have nothing behind it, we'll tell you that too instead of stringing you along.

sections.heading: This Is Michigan Basin Ground, Not Antrim Core
paragraphs: Wellston sits well outside the dense Antrim Shale core that runs through Otsego, Kalkaska, and Antrim counties. Manistee County's oil and gas history is tied more to the broader Michigan Basin — shallow Dundee limestone oil production going back to the mid-1900s, along with scattered deeper exploration over the decades. Drilling density around Wellston specifically has historically been light, largely because so much of the surrounding land sits inside the Manistee National Forest, which limits where wells can go.

That changes the conversation compared to a core Antrim county. Instead of assuming there's a producing well tied to every parcel, the real first question for a Wellston interest is whether there's been any drilling activity near your specific legal description at all.

sections.heading: Prairie du Chien and Deeper Basin Potential
paragraphs: Parts of the Michigan Basin, including areas of Manistee County, have seen exploration interest in the deeper Prairie du Chien and Trenton-Black River formations over the years, targets that sit thousands of feet below the shallow Antrim gas zone. These deeper plays see periodic bursts of leasing activity when operators think the economics work, then go quiet for years at a time. If your family holds an old lease from one of those active stretches, it's worth finding out whether it's still held by production or has expired.
We check lease status against county records before telling you anything about value, because an expired lease with no current well changes the picture entirely from an active, producing one.

sections.heading: Old Timber-Land Severances Are Common Around Here
paragraphs: A lot of the land bordering the national forest near Wellston was logged and sold off in pieces a century or more ago, and mineral rights got severed from the surface in the process — sometimes on paper that's hard to read by modern standards. Manistee County's register of deeds holds the record, but matching an old severance deed to a current legal description can take some work.

If you've inherited something like this and have no idea whether it's even active, that's a normal starting point for us. We can usually tell you within a day or two whether there's a lease or production tied to what you hold.

faqs.question: Is there active drilling near Wellston right now?
faqs.answer: Drilling density around Wellston is light compared to the Antrim core counties, partly because of the surrounding national forest land. We check your specific parcel before saying anything definite about activity.

faqs.question: My old lease might be expired. Does that matter?
faqs.answer: Yes, significantly. An expired lease with no current well is valued very differently than an active producing interest. We verify status against county records first.

faqs.question: I'm not even sure what I own. Can you help figure that out?
faqs.answer: Yes. Send whatever deed or paperwork you have and we'll work with Manistee County records to figure out what it actually maps to.
